programs.sol:
"""Approximate a negative response to common general-purpose nouns.

Training peaks included duration, manner and reason expressions. This small
semantic lexicon uses WordNet inflections/time categories and word frequency;
the immediately preceding word changes its strength. Nominal "while", scalar
"long/far", and nominal endings have separate rules. Alphabetic fragments are
joined up to 40 characters, with state cleared at document boundaries. This
leaves word-specific amplitudes and most multilingual responses unexplained.
"""
from functools import lru_cache
import re
import wordnet
from wordfreq import zipf_frequency

READS = ()
NOUN_GROUPS = {
    'manner': set(('way manner means method approach fashion style strategy '
                   'basis course mode procedure practice').split()),
    'reason': set('reason purpose cause motive aim goal intention'.split()),
    'general_thing': set(('thing stuff matter case issue problem question '
                          'situation circumstance event accident mishap').split()),
    'action': set(('action measure step effort attempt help care thought '
                   'decision choice plan duty obligation attention').split()),
    'quantity': set(('amount quantity bit lot enough number degree extent '
                     'portion part proportion share').split()),
    'thought': set('idea sense point view fact belief opinion knowledge'.split()),
}
DETERMINERS = set(('a an the this that these those each every any some no '
                    'another other such').split())
POSSESSIVES = set('my your our their his her its whose'.split())
DURATION_MODIFIERS = set(('long short brief little considerable extended '
                         'lengthy prolonged regular timely').split())

# Per-class offset and slope against English word frequency above Zipf 4.
SEMANTICS = {
    'action': (-0.2527, 0.0159),
    'duration': (0.0619, -0.1135),
    'general_thing': (-0.0781, -0.0091),
    'manner': (-0.0942, -0.1049),
    'quantity': (-0.1060, 0.0250),
    'reason': (-0.1169, -0.1732),
    'thought': (-0.0982, 0.0346),
    'time': (-0.0398, 0.0198),
}
@lru_cache(maxsize=65536)
def noun_score(word):
    if word == 'while':
        return 0.0  # usually a conjunction; its nominal use is handled below
    bases = set(wordnet.base_forms(word, 'noun')) | {word}
    flags = {name: bool(bases & members)
             for name, members in NOUN_GROUPS.items()}
    flags['time'] = 'noun.time' in wordnet.categories(word)
    flags['duration'] = (flags['time']
                         and wordnet.is_a(word, 'time period'))
    if not any(flags.values()):
        return 0.0
    frequency = max(0.0, zipf_frequency(word, 'en') - 4.0)
    return sum(offset + slope * frequency
               for name, (offset, slope) in SEMANTICS.items() if flags[name])


@lru_cache(maxsize=65536)
def context_strength(previous):
    return (1 + 1.052 * ('adjective' in wordnet.parts_of_speech(previous))
            + 0.559 * (previous in DETERMINERS)
            + 0.338 * (previous in POSSESSIVES)
            + 0.348 * (previous in DURATION_MODIFIERS))


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    document = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if carry is None or carry[0] != document:
        old, previous = '', ''
    else:
        old, previous = carry[1:]
    text = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    stripped = text.strip()
    if text.isalpha():
        word = (old + text.lower())[-40:]
        previous = previous if old else ''
    elif stripped.isalpha():
        word, previous = stripped.lower(), old
    else:
        match = re.search(r'([^\W\d_]+)$', text)
        word, previous = (match.group(0).lower() if match else ''), ''
    state = (document, word, previous)
    value = 0.0
    if not word:
        return state, value
    value += context_strength(previous) * noun_score(word)
    # A nominal duration, rather than the conjunction "while".
    if word == 'while' and (previous in DETERMINERS or
                            previous in DURATION_MODIFIERS):
        value -= 1.255
    if word in {'far', 'long'}:
        value -= 0.116
        if previous in {'so', 'as', 'too', 'how', 'very'}:
            value -= 0.599
    if len(word) > 4:
        if word.endswith((
            'ness', 'nesses', 'ity', 'ities', 'ance', 'ances', 'ence', 'ences',
            'tion', 'tions', 'sion', 'sions', 'ment', 'ments', 'ship')):
            value -= 0.033
        if word.endswith((
            'ción', 'ciones', 'ção', 'ções', 'zioni', 'dade', 'dades',
            'idad', 'idades', 'ité', 'ités', 'ità', 'mento', 'mentos')):
            value -= 0.121
    return state, float(value)

"""Activation of layers.1.mlp.down_proj:1984, a feature that goes negative.

It turns on at the head noun of an adverbial phrase of time, duration, manner,
reason, effort, chance, circumstance or attitude: "for a long time", "in this
manner", "for some reason", "the best way to", "under no circumstances",
"with gratitude", "at the moment", "a matter of minutes". It is strongest on
such a noun right after a preposition or a modifier ("for a long time",
"the best way"), and weaker on the same noun elsewhere. Degree and duration
adverbs ("soon", "enough", "far", "ago", "long") get a weak version.

It does not fire on abstract nouns in general ("freedom", "system", "problem")
or on concrete nouns ("house", "car"), and it is near zero on ordinary time
adverbs ("today", "later", "always").

The program predicts a negative number: -0.6 for a listed noun preceded within
three words by a preposition or directly by a modifier, -0.3 for the same noun
otherwise, and -0.3 for the degree adverbs. Everything else is 0.
"""

READS = ()

TIME = set("""time times year years day days week weeks month months decade decades moment
moments instant period periods duration hour hours minute minutes seconds night nights
season seasons weekend""".split())
MANNER = set("way ways manner manners fashion approach means method methods extent degree".split())
REASON = set("""reason reasons basis cause purpose motive explanation idea opinion intention
intentions aim""".split())
EFFORT = set("""effort efforts action actions step steps measure measures attempt attempts
endeavor endeavors determination dedication responsibility decision choice""".split())
CHANCE = set("""chance chances possibility possibilities opportunity occasion occasions incident
instances""".split())
CIRCUMSTANCE = set("""circumstance circumstances situation situations condition conditions
scenario""".split())
ATTITUDE = set("""attention regard regards respect consideration care discretion gratitude
thanks mind sight thought notice""".split())
FEELING = set("""shame pride fright shock regret joy hope surprise excitement confusion courage
luck fortune trouble patience""".split())
VAGUE = set("thing things matter amount bit".split())
TRANSLATED = set("""zeit temps tiempo momento manera forma modo moyen raison heure hora jour dia
vez waktu tempo 時間 时间 方法 方式 способ времени""".split())
NOUNS = (TIME | MANNER | REASON | EFFORT | CHANCE | CIRCUMSTANCE | ATTITUDE | FEELING
         | VAGUE | TRANSLATED)
DEGREE_ADVERBS = set("soon enough far ago long longer".split())
PREPOSITIONS = set("of for in to at on with by from into over under without".split())
MODIFIERS = set("long short good best reasonable timely regular great few considerable".split())


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    word = prefix.token_strings[-1].strip().lower()
    if word in DEGREE_ADVERBS:
        return None, -0.3
    if word not in NOUNS:
        return None, 0.0
    before = [s.strip().lower() for s in prefix.token_strings[-4:-1]]
    previous = before[-1] if before else ""
    if any(w in PREPOSITIONS for w in before) or previous in MODIFIERS:
        return None, -0.6
    return None, -0.3

"""Layer 1, MLP down-projection component 1985: a "padding and ASCII-art" detector.

It fires on the whitespace and repeated-symbol tokens that lay out text visually:
  * long runs of spaces or tabs (12+ characters): padding, column alignment, or the
    blank part of a text diagram;
  * shorter runs of spaces that sit mid-line, after visible text on the same line
    (spacing inside a table or ASCII art); only weakly when the run is ordinary
    indentation at the start of a line;
  * whitespace that ends a line (a padded blank line inside a diagram);
  * runs of 4+ identical art symbols (* ^ _ ~ - =), optionally after one space: the
    stars of a drawn shape, the caret underline under a compiler error, rules and borders.
Everything else (words, digits, ordinary punctuation, code indentation) is about zero.

The only state carried along the row is whether the current line already has visible
text, reset at each newline and at each document boundary.
"""

READS = ()

LONG_RUN = 12              # a run of spaces/tabs this long or longer is "long padding"
ART_CHARS = set("*^_~-=")  # symbols that draw borders, underlines and shapes


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    s = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    new_doc = len(prefix.document_ids) > 1 and prefix.document_ids[-2] != prefix.document_ids[-1]
    text_seen = bool(carry) and not new_doc  # visible text earlier on this line
    blank = s.strip() == ""
    core = s.lstrip(" ")
    if s.isspace() and "\n" not in s and len(s) >= 4:
        value = 1.5 if len(s) >= LONG_RUN else (0.8 if text_seen else 0.2)
    elif "\n" in s and blank and len(s) >= 4:
        value = 1.3  # whitespace that ends a line, inside a padded block
    elif len(core) >= 4 and len(set(core)) == 1 and core[0] in ART_CHARS:
        value = 2.0  # ****, ^^^^, ____, ====
    else:
        value = 0.0
    # update the line state with this token
    if "\n" in s:
        text_seen = s.split("\n")[-1].strip() != ""
    else:
        text_seen = text_seen or not blank
    return text_seen, float(value)

programs.sol:
"""A local-template approximation, not a single semantic category.

Recognize stock source-code headers, license clauses and website labels.
A few token-shape priors apply at document starts. Everything else is zero;
small, idiosyncratic lexical responses are deliberately not tabulated.
"""
READS = ()

# Current token: (recognizable text ending at that token, response).
FRAGMENTS = {
    # Source-code and document-format scaffolding.
    ' b': ('+++ b', 1.9),
    ' EXISTS': ('TABLE IF EXISTS', 1.0),
    ' charset': ('text/html; charset', -3.0),
    ' std': ('using namespace std', 1.8),
    'esModule': ('"__esModule', 1.45),
    'adge': ('shields.io/badge', 1.1),
    ' for': ('# Definition for', 1.45),
    # Copyright, permission and IDE boilerplate.
    ' rights': ('limitation the rights', 1.5),
    ' License': ('limitations under the License', -1.3),
    ' Templates': ('Tools | Templates', -1.65),
    's': ('Copyrights', 2.1),
    # Stock labels on forums, reference pages and document-hosting sites.
    ' forums': ('these public forums', -1.25),
    ' Customers': ('Satisfied Customers', -2.4),
    ' User': ('Wiki User', -1.0),
    'Share': ('SlideShare', -2.6),
    ' Measurements': ('Weights and Measurements', -0.34),
    ' context': ('Sequence in context', -0.43),
    ' px': ('Size: px', 1.58),
    ' reply': ('Latest reply', -0.42),
    ' Info': ('Tag Info', 1.15),
    " '": ("Discussion in '", -1.8),
    ' Corrections': ('Suggest Corrections', -0.44),
    ' App': ('Open in App', -0.87),
    ' directed': ('examiner should be directed', 0.65),
    ' solution': ('already-completed solution', 0.95),
}


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    tail = carry[1] if carry is not None and carry[0] == doc else ''
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    text = tail + token
    value = 0.0
    if not tail:
        if len(token) == 1 and token.isascii() and token.isupper():
            value = 0.66
        elif token.istitle() and token.isascii():
            value = 0.20
        elif token.strip().isdigit():
            value = 0.16
        if token == '#':
            value = 0.83
        elif token == '##':
            value = 1.32
        elif token == '<|endoftext|>':
            value = -1.34

    fragment = FRAGMENTS.get(token)
    if fragment is not None and text.endswith(fragment[0]):
        value = fragment[1]
    if token == ':' and tail == '---\ntitle':
        value = 6.0
    elif token == ' \u200b\u200b':
        value = -3.7 if tail.endswith(' values') else -2.0
    elif token == 'UTC' and tail.endswith('\xa0'):
        value = -2.8
    elif tail.endswith('using System'):
        if token == '.Drawing' and '.Data;' in tail:
            value = 2.5
        elif token == '.Data' and '.ComponentModel;' in tail:
            value = 1.7
        elif token == '.Text' and tail.endswith(
            'using System;\nusing System.Collections.Generic;\nusing System'
        ):
            value = 1.55
    elif token == '.TextView' and tail.endswith('import android.widget'):
        value = 0.7
    elif token == '.xlim' and tail.endswith('plt') and 'lw=2)' in tail:
        value = 1.95
    return (doc, text[-240:]), value

"""A coarse position-and-spelling approximation, not a semantic trigger.

The strongest simple pattern in training is a negative document-initial
activation, especially for longer tokens. Elsewhere the prediction is
small: it distinguishes short word continuations from new words and
long Latin-script tokens from other long tokens. These are group means;
most of this component's token-specific variation remains unexplained.
"""

import unicodedata

READS = ()


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    document = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    position = 0 if carry is None or carry[0] != document else carry[1] + 1
    carry = (document, position)
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    word = token.strip()
    short = len(word) <= 3

    if position == 0:
        return carry, -0.094 if short else -0.214
    if position <= 3:
        return carry, -0.036 if word.isdigit() else -0.006

    if short:
        previous = prefix.token_strings[-2]
        continuation = bool(token and previous and token[0].isalpha()
                            and previous[-1].isalpha())
        return carry, 0.0064 if continuation else 0.0002

    latin = any('LATIN' in unicodedata.name(c, '') for c in word)
    return carry, 0.0062 if latin else -0.0086
programs.haiku:
"""Layer-1 MLP down-projection component 1988: a document-start detector.

What it does: this component is almost silent. Its activation is small noise
(std about 0.05) around zero almost everywhere. The one consistent pattern is at
the first token of each document (the start of a row, or the token right after a
document boundary inside a packed row): there the activation is reliably negative,
about -0.14 on average, with spread (std about 0.3). Elsewhere it is near zero.

So the program predicts a fixed negative value on document-start tokens and zero
on every other token. It ignores token identity. Its CI is essentially zero
everywhere, so switching it off changes the model's output very little.
"""

READS = ()

DOC_START_VALUE = -0.14   # mean activation on the first token of a document
OTHER_VALUE = 0.0         # mean activation elsewhere (near zero)


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    t = prefix.position
    starts_document = t == 0 or prefix.document_ids[t] != prefix.document_ids[t - 1]
    return None, (DOC_START_VALUE if starts_document else OTHER_VALUE)

"""Component layers.1.mlp.down_proj:1989 as a copula detector.

What it does: fires on the finite forms of the verb "to be" (is, are, was, were, am, and
their French/Italian/German/Portuguese/Polish equivalents est, ist, è, war, sono, jest)
when they link a subject to its predicate. It is strongest when the subject is a thing or
an idea ("The problem is", "This is", "It was", "the issue is"), and weak or absent when
the subject is a person pronoun ("I am", "we are", "they were") or the existential
"there is". It is also stronger in running English prose than in code or data lists, where
"is" is a label or operator. "'s" fires when it contracts "is" after "it", "this", "that",
"what" or "which" ("It's", "That's"). A bare past participle at the very start of a row,
with no context, also fires, since the model reads it as a predicate with no subject.

Why: the copula is the main thing this component writes, and the other cases are its
clearest exceptions. Everything else is predicted as 0.
"""

import re

READS = ()

COPULA = {"is", "are", "was", "were", "am", "est", "ist", "jest", "è", "war", "sono"}
PERSON = {"i", "we", "you", "he", "she", "they", "me", "us", "them"}
THING = {"it", "this", "that", "which", "what", "here"}
WORD = re.compile(r"^ ?[A-Za-z]+[.,]?$")


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    word = prefix.token_strings[-1].strip().lower()
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if prefix.position == 0:
        # No context at a row's start: a bare past participle reads as a predicate.
        is_participle = word.endswith("ed") and word.isalpha() and len(word) > 3
        return None, 2.5 if is_participle else 0.0
    prev = ""
    if prefix.document_ids[-2] == doc:
        prev = prefix.token_strings[-2].strip().lower()
    if word in COPULA:
        # Person subjects and "there" give little; other subjects give the full value.
        strength = 0.1 if prev in PERSON or prev == "there" else 0.7
        # Prose context (mostly English words in the last 16 tokens) scales it down in code.
        window = [s for s, d in zip(prefix.token_strings[-17:-1], prefix.document_ids[-17:-1]) if d == doc]
        prose = sum(1 for s in window if WORD.match(s)) / max(1, len(window))
        return None, strength * (0.3 + 0.7 * prose)
    if word in {"'s", "’s"} and prev in THING:
        return None, 0.8
    return None, 0.0

"""Layer 1, MLP down-projection, component 1991: a sparse word detector.

What it does, in plain terms. Most of the time this component is near zero. It
responds to a short list of words and characters:

  * the name ".NET": the token "net" or "NET" right after a dot ("Dot.Net",
    "java.net", ".NET Core"), and the tokens ".net" / ".NET" themselves. Strongest.
  * the Chinese characters for calm, quiet and clean: 宁 寧 静 靜 净 淨 (peace,
    quiet, clean), plus a few characters that co-occur with them in the data
    (凌 凝 停 靖 凭, and weaker 冷 憑). Strong on 宁 寧 静 靜 净 淨.
  * the web and file-name suffixes ".github" and ".config" (weak), and ".org",
    ".com", ".php" (very weak).
  * the first token of every document (where the text has no context yet), which
    is mildly negative.

Everything else predicts 0. The small wiggles around 0 are not predictable from the
token alone, so the program does not try to reproduce them.
"""

from collections.abc import Mapping

READS = ()

DOT_NET = 4.5  # ".NET" as a name
CALM_STRONG = 4.5  # 宁 寧 静 靜 净 淨
CALM_WEAK = 3.0  # 凌 凝 停 靖 凭
CALM_FAINT = 1.0  # 冷 憑
CALM = {
    **dict.fromkeys("宁寧静靜净淨", CALM_STRONG),
    **dict.fromkeys("凌凝停靖凭", CALM_WEAK),
    **dict.fromkeys("冷憑", CALM_FAINT),
}
DOT_NET_TOKENS = (".net", ".NET", ".Net")
DOT_NET_WORDS = ("net", "NET", "Net")
CONFIG_TOKENS = (".github", ".config")
SUFFIX_TOKENS = (".org", ".com", ".php", ".edu")
DOCUMENT_START = -0.2  # first token of a document


def step(carry, prefix, upstream: Mapping):
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    previous = prefix.token_strings[-2] if len(prefix) > 1 else ""
    new_document = len(prefix) == 1 or prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]
    if new_document:
        value = DOCUMENT_START
    elif token in DOT_NET_TOKENS:
        value = DOT_NET
    elif token.strip() in DOT_NET_WORDS and previous.endswith((".", "Dot", "dot")):
        value = DOT_NET
    elif token in CALM:
        value = CALM[token]
    elif token in CONFIG_TOKENS:
        value = 0.7
    elif token in SUFFIX_TOKENS:
        value = 0.2
    else:
        value = 0.0
    return carry, float(value)

"""layers.1.mlp.down_proj:1993: a chat / tool markup detector.

The component writes a large negative value on the special control tokens that structure a
conversation and its tool calls, and is close to zero on ordinary text:

  <|im_start|>      about -4.1   opens each chat turn ("user", "assistant", ...)
  <tool_response>   about -3.0   opens tool output
  </tool_response>  about -3.7   closes tool output
  <tool_call>       about -2.1   opens a tool call
  </tool_call>      about -2.6   closes a tool call
  <think>           about -3.9   opens reasoning
  </think>          about -1.5   closes reasoning
  <|im_end|>        about +0.15  ends a turn (barely active)

Two context effects: a <|im_start|> that begins a document (right after <|endoftext|>, or
first in a packed row) is only about -0.6, and the first token of any document is mildly
negative (about -0.25). Everything else is about 0.

Predicting these values captures most of the component's variance and nearly all of its
effect on the model's next-token predictions; the small diffuse activity on ordinary
tokens (about 0.03 in size) is not modelled.
"""

READS = ()

CONTROL_TOKENS = {
    "<|im_start|>": -4.1,
    "<tool_response>": -3.0,
    "</tool_response>": -3.7,
    "<tool_call>": -2.1,
    "</tool_call>": -2.6,
    "<think>": -3.9,
    "</think>": -1.5,
    "<|im_end|>": 0.15,
}
DOC_START_IM_START = -0.6
DOC_START_OTHER = -0.25


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    t = prefix.position
    doc_start = t == 0 or prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]
    if doc_start:
        if token == "<|im_start|>":
            return carry, DOC_START_IM_START
        return carry, DOC_START_OTHER
    return carry, CONTROL_TOKENS.get(token, 0.0)

"""layers.1.mlp.down_proj:1994 — a document-start detector for the first token.

What it does
------------
The component's activation is almost entirely a function of the FIRST token of a
document. A "document" here is a run of tokens with one document id; rows are packed
with several documents, and a row may begin mid-document, so position 0 of a row
counts too. At a document's first token, attention can only see that token itself, so
the component's value depends only on which token it is.

Nonzero values are assigned by the kind of first token:
  * end-of-text marker <|endoftext|>        strongly positive (about +7.7)
  * line breaks, spaces, punctuation, digits  positive (about +2.3 to +2.8)
    (digits 0 and 9 are the exception: about 0)
  * function words (a, the, of, to, and, with, by, can, not...) and single lowercase
    letters (n, x, m...)                        positive (about +2.3 to +2.6)
  * pronouns and auxiliary verbs (is, it, your, this, they...)  weakly positive (+1.2)
  * ordinary words, names, non-Latin words     weakly positive (about +0.5)
  * chat / tool markup (<|im_start|>, <tool_call>, <think>...)  negative (about -1.5)
A document's second token gets +2.0 when it repeats the first token.
Every other position predicts 0: the component is nearly silent there.

The values are class averages taken from the component's activation on each token
type at a document start, weighted by how often each token occurs.
"""

READS = ()

END_OF_TEXT = "<|endoftext|>"
CHAT_MARKUP = ("<|", "<tool", "</tool", "<think", "</think")
FUNCTION_WORDS = set(
    " a an the of to and in for with by that as or on at from can not but if when "
    "some such also".split()
)
PRONOUNS_AUX = set(
    " is was are were be it he she we they i my his her its their your you this these "
    "them me our has have had will would should may do does".split()
)


def first_token_value(token):
    """Activation predicted when `token` is the first token of a document."""
    core = token.strip()
    if core == END_OF_TEXT:
        return 7.7
    if core.startswith(CHAT_MARKUP):
        return -1.5
    if len(token) == 1 and token.islower():
        return 2.6
    if not core:
        return 2.8  # spaces and line breaks
    if not any(ch.isalpha() for ch in core):
        if core in ("0", "9"):
            return 0.0  # the exceptions among digits
        return 2.3  # punctuation, symbols, other digits
    if core in FUNCTION_WORDS:
        return 2.3
    if core in PRONOUNS_AUX:
        return 1.2
    if core[0].isupper() or not all(ord(ch) < 128 for ch in core):
        return 0.55  # capitalised words and non-Latin scripts
    return 0.5  # other ordinary lowercase words


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    """Carry = (position where this document began, its first token id)."""
    position = prefix.position
    if position == 0 or prefix.document_ids[-2] != prefix.document_ids[-1]:
        carry = (position, prefix.token_ids[-1])
        return carry, first_token_value(prefix.token_strings[-1])
    start, first = carry
    if position - start == 1 and prefix.token_ids[-1] == first:
        return carry, 2.0  # second token repeats the first
    return carry, 0.0

"""A sparse boundary/onset detector with secondary Chinese lexical responses.

Message endings are positive, less so immediately after tool blocks. The first
visible token of each row or packed document has a separate offset, retained
while that token repeats. Initial formatting runs and the initial digits '12'
have several large, narrow responses. Some declaration keywords are negative.

Separate Chinese branches recognize tradition, feelings, influence, material
entities, standards, additive connectives and 'not yet'. These are lexical
responses, not a claim that all words with those meanings behave alike.
Unrecognized ordinary text is approximated by zero.
"""
import unicodedata
from opencc import OpenCC

"""Coarse approximation of Chinese constructions spanning token boundaries.

AABB reduplication and quantity phrases receive positive values. Connective,
negated, directional and institutional compounds receive negative values.
For other two-character tokens, dictionary completions suggest a negative
correction, while unfinished or overlapping words suggest a positive one.
Frequencies filter out poorly attested combinations. Two document-initial
metadata labels have separate rules.

These are conservative pattern averages: most lexical variation, including
arbitrary activations at a document's first token, remains unexplained.
"""
from functools import lru_cache
import regex
import cedict
import opencc
import wordfreq

READS = ()
_SIMPLIFY = opencc.OpenCC('t2s')
_FREQUENCIES = wordfreq.get_frequency_dict('zh')
# Prefixes of dictionary words, not a learned list of token combinations.
_PREFIXES = set()
for _word in cedict._table()[1]:
    if 3 <= len(_word) <= 6 and regex.fullmatch(r'\p{Han}+', _word):
        _PREFIXES.update(_word[:i] for i in range(2, len(_word)))


@lru_cache(maxsize=50000)
def boundary(previous, token):
    if not regex.fullmatch(r'\p{Han}+', token):
        return 0.0
    if not previous or not regex.search(r'\p{Han}$', previous):
        return 0.0
    previous = _SIMPLIFY.convert(previous).strip()
    token = _SIMPLIFY.convert(token).strip()
    joined = previous[-1] + token
    whole = bool(cedict.glosses(joined))
    if token in ('而', '而是') and cedict.glosses(previous[-1] + '而'):
        return -1.15
    if token in ('下', '下的', '下一'):
        if cedict.glosses(previous[-1] + '下') or previous[-1] in '往向':
            return -0.5
    if len(token) >= 2 and token.startswith('不') and any(
            cedict.glosses(previous[-n:] + token)
            or _FREQUENCIES.get(previous[-n:] + token, 0) > 0
            for n in range(1, min(3, len(previous)) + 1)):
        return -0.45
    # Government, courts, ministers and chairpersons inside a larger word.
    if token in {'政府', '法院', '部长', '主席'} and whole:
        return -0.8
    if len(token) != 2:
        return 0.0
    a, b = token
    if previous[-1] == a:
        repeated = a + a + b + b
        if cedict.glosses(repeated) or _FREQUENCIES.get(repeated, 0) > 0:
            return 1.3
    if previous[-1] == '数' and regex.fullmatch('[十百千][万亿]', token):
        return 1.1
    # Distributive phrases about steps or portions, rather than calendar units.
    if previous[-1] in '每逐' and token in ('一分', '一步'):
        return 0.9
    # Frequencies here are occurrences per million words.
    joined_frequency = 1_000_000 * _FREQUENCIES.get(joined, 0)
    if whole and joined_frequency > 0.04:
        common = 1_000_000 * _FREQUENCIES.get(token, 0) >= 60
        return -0.25 if common else -0.10
    if joined in _PREFIXES and not cedict.glosses(joined):
        return 0.29
    overlap = previous[-1] + token[0]
    if (len(previous) == 1 and cedict.glosses(overlap)
            and _FREQUENCIES.get(overlap, 0) > 0):
        return 0.10
    return 0.0


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    new_doc = carry is None or carry[0] != doc
    previous = '' if new_doc else carry[1]
    position = 0 if new_doc else carry[2] + 1
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    if position == 1 and token == 'filename' and previous == '<':
        value = -1.6
    elif position == 1 and token == ':' and previous == 'Title':
        value = 0.75
    else:
        value = boundary(previous, token)
    return (doc, token, position), value

"""layers.1.mlp.down_proj:2000 - a weak, document-start detector.

This component's contribution is small and diffuse: its activation is a noisy,
token-specific readout with no concentrated concept behind it. Most of its variance
sits in one place that a person can name: the first token of a document (or of a
packed row), where the model's attention can see nothing but that token. There the
activation is clearly positive on average, with a size that depends on what kind of
token starts the document: about +0.10 for an unspaced English word, +0.15 for a
Chinese character, +0.13 for a digit or a whitespace/newline token, and 0 otherwise.
Everywhere else the program predicts 0.

A document start is a position where the document id changes, or the first position
of a row. Both are reset points for the model, so both are treated alike.
"""

READS = ()


def kind_value(token):
    """Typical activation at a document's first token, by the kind of token."""
    if token.strip() == "":
        return 0.13
    if token[0] != " " and token.isascii() and token.isalpha():
        return 0.10
    if token.strip().isdigit():
        return 0.13
    if any("一" <= ch <= "鿿" for ch in token):
        return 0.15
    return 0.0


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    t = prefix.position
    starts_doc = t == 0 or prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]
    if not starts_doc:
        return None, 0.0
    return None, kind_value(prefix.token_strings[-1])

"""layers.1.mlp.down_proj:2001: the "in" detector.

What it does: this component goes strongly negative on the word "in" when it is used as
a preposition that introduces a place or a time ("born in 1950", "built in 1880",
"in the end", "in Moscow"). It also does so for the same word in other languages:
"в" (Russian), "en" (Spanish), "em" (Portuguese), "w" (Polish), "în" (Romanian),
"im" (German), "dans" (French), "nel" (Italian), "trong" (Vietnamese), "في" (Arabic), "در" (Persian).
Everything else sits near zero, except a steady positive value on runs of dot leaders.

The program is a lookup on the current token, with two exceptions: "results in",
"resulting in" stay near zero, because there "in" introduces a consequence and does not
locate anything; and "····" dot leaders get a fixed positive value. It reads only the
newest token and the one before it.

The values are typical activations, rounded from the training data. Within each word the
spread is large (for "in" about 0.65), and this program does not model it.
"""

ENGLISH_IN = {" in": -1.6, " In": -1.7, "In": -1.7, " IN": -0.95}

# The same word in other languages, with typical values.
OTHER_LANGUAGE_IN = {
    " в": -2.9, " В": -3.1, "В": -2.9,               # Russian, Bulgarian
    " en": -2.4, " En": -2.5, " em": -2.4, " Em": -1.1,  # Spanish, French; Portuguese
    " im": -1.4, " în": -2.7, " w": -0.9,           # German; Romanian; Polish
    " dans": -0.9, " nel": -1.8, " trong": -1.8,    # French; Italian; Vietnamese
    " في": -1.3, " در": -3.0, "在": -0.6,           # Arabic; Persian; Chinese
}

IN_WORDS = {**ENGLISH_IN, **OTHER_LANGUAGE_IN}

# "results in", "resulting in": "in" here introduces a consequence, so it stays near zero.
RESULT_WORDS = {" result", " results", " resulted", " resulting"}

DOT_LEADER = "··"
DOT_LEADER_VALUE = 2.1


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    tokens = prefix.token_strings
    token = tokens[-1]
    before = tokens[-2] if len(tokens) > 1 else ""
    if token in IN_WORDS:

"""layers.1.mlp.down_proj:2002 — a whitespace and document-boundary detector.

What the component does: it is almost silent on ordinary words, but it responds to
whitespace and to the boundaries between documents. In plain terms:

- The end-of-text token <|endoftext|> gives a strong positive value (about +1.4).
- The first token of each document (the token after <|endoftext|>, or the first token of
  a row) gives a weak positive value (about +0.15).
- A tab that comes right after a space (mixed space/tab indentation, or a tab after a
  space in running text) gives a strong negative value (about -5.5). This is the
  component's biggest and most reliable response.
- A bare tab (nothing else but tabs) right after a digit gives a moderate positive value
  (about +0.9). This is the tab that follows a line number in numbered code listings.
- A very long run of spaces (28 or more) after other whitespace, such as the indentation
  that follows a tab or a line number, gives a negative value (about -2.5).
- A run of two or more spaces in the middle of a line, right after a letter or
  punctuation mark (column padding inside a line), gives a small positive value (about +0.5).
- Everything else, including ordinary words and single spaces, gives 0.

END_OF_TEXT = "<|endoftext|>"
PADDING_AFTER = "ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZabcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz.,;:!?)]}\"'"


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    previous = prefix.token_strings[-2] if len(prefix.token_strings) > 1 else ""

    # Document boundaries.
    if token == END_OF_TEXT:
        return None, 1.44
    if len(prefix.token_strings) == 1 or prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]:
        return None, 0.15

    if "\t" in token:

            return None, -5.5

    # A bare tab right after a digit: a line-number gutter ("  139<TAB>") before code.
    if token.strip("\t") == "" and token.startswith("\t") and previous[-1:].isdigit():
        return None, 0.9

    # Runs of spaces.
    if len(token) >= 2 and token.strip(" ") == "":
        if len(token) >= 28 and previous.strip(" \t") == "":
            return None, -2.5
        if previous[-1:] and previous[-1] in PADDING_AFTER:
            return None, 0.5

    return None, 0.0

"""Document-opener detector for layers.1.mlp.down_proj:2004.

What the component does, in plain terms: it is silent almost everywhere. It
speaks only at the first token of a document, meaning the token right after an
<|endoftext|> separator or the first token of a packed row. There it writes a
value that depends on what that token is, and the strongest response goes to
tokens that open a source file, a comment block, or a markup/SQL block:
  "package", "using", "import", "#include", "namespace", "const" (file headers)
  "/*", "/**", "//", "#!/", "<?", "<div", "@Override", "--"        (comments, tags)
Other code keywords ("def", "class", "function") respond weakly, ordinary
English or other word openers respond a little, and fragments of Cyrillic text
go slightly negative. Mid-document tokens predict 0; a weak mid-document term
only made the fit worse.

Why: the component is a "this document looks like code or markup from its first
token" signal, read off the token alone (the first token attends only to itself,
so its value is fixed by its identity).

Main program: step() finds whether the current token starts a document, then
looks its text up in the tiers below.

import re

READS = ()

# Tier values (approximate activations at a document start).
FILE_HEADER_VALUE = 24.0   # tokens that open a source file's header
COMMENT_TAG_VALUE = 13.0   # comment, shebang, preprocessor, markup, annotation openers
OTHER_CODE_VALUE = 6.0     # other programming / SQL keywords
WORD_VALUE = 2.5           # ordinary words at a document start
CHAT_TAG_VALUE = 3.0       # chat-template markers such as <|im_start|>
OTHER_VALUE = 1.0          # digits, punctuation, CJK, other scripts
CYRILLIC_VALUE = -0.5      # Cyrillic fragments

FILE_HEADER = set(
    "package using import from include namespace public private const export use "
    "#include #import #pragma".split()
)
OTHER_CODE = set(
    "def class function var let require module library declare typedef interface "
    "static void struct enum func fn select create drop alter insert update delete "
    "table where begin int return extern define".split()
)
COMMENT_OR_TAG = re.compile(r"(/\*|//|#!|#[a-z]|<\?|<[a-zA-Z!]|@[A-Za-z]|--|\"\"\"|'''|\(\*|\{-)")
CYRILLIC = re.compile(r"[Ѐ-ӿ]")
WORD = re.compile(r" ?[A-Za-z]+")


def opener_value(text: str) -> float:
    """Activation for a document's first token, from its text alone."""
    text = text.lstrip("﻿")  # a byte-order mark may precede the first token
    if text == "":
        return OTHER_VALUE
    if CYRILLIC.search(text):
        return CYRILLIC_VALUE
    if text.startswith("<|"):
        return CHAT_TAG_VALUE
    if text == "#":
        return WORD_VALUE
    if not text.startswith(" "):
        if text in FILE_HEADER:
            return FILE_HEADER_VALUE
        if COMMENT_OR_TAG.match(text):
            return COMMENT_TAG_VALUE
        if text in OTHER_CODE:
            return OTHER_CODE_VALUE
    if WORD.fullmatch(text):
        return WORD_VALUE
    return OTHER_VALUE


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    t = prefix.position
    starts_document = t == 0 or prefix.document_ids[t] != prefix.document_ids[t - 1]
    if not starts_document:
        return None, 0.0
    return None, float(opener_value(prefix.token_strings[t]))

This component writes (negatively) on the whitespace that indents a line of code
when the line break before it has been replaced by something else:

1. Numbered listings ("  37<TAB>    code"): a tab right after a line number.

2. Escaped newlines inside strings ("...\\n    code", a literal backslash-n):

"""A French accented-vowel spelling signal.

Circumflex pieces are negative, especially in French words and French context.
The signal weakens for following letters already bundled into the token.
Letters in the next token can retain a weaker accent signal. Function-word
counts distinguish French from Vietnamese, which uses some of the same vowels.
A separate small positive signal marks x appended to a word, with a larger one
for the x suffix of DOCX documents. Everything else is zero.
"""
import re
import unicodedata
from wordfreq import top_n_list

READS = ()
CIRCUMFLEX = 'âêîôû'
FRENCH = frozenset('''le les des du une est sont dans pour avec aux qui pas
nous vous leur leurs cette ces cet sur'''.split())
VIETNAMESE = frozenset('''của và các những trong một người không được là có
với cho này đã từ tôi'''.split())
WORD_END = re.compile(r'[^\W\d_]+$')

# Prefixes that have reached the circumflex in a common French spelling.
FRENCH_SPELLINGS = set()
for spelling in top_n_list('fr', 20000):
    if spelling.isalpha():
        for i, letter in enumerate(spelling):
            if letter in CIRCUMFLEX:
                FRENCH_SPELLINGS.update(
                    spelling[:j] for j in range(i + 1, len(spelling) + 1)
                )


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    document = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if carry is None or carry[0] != document:
        carry = (document, '', '', 0.0, 0.0)
    _, old_word, previous, french, vietnamese = carry
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1].lower()
    french = .94 * french + (token.strip() in FRENCH)
    vietnamese = .94 * vietnamese + (token.strip() in VIETNAMESE)
    fr = float(french > .7)
    vi = float(vietnamese > .7)
    match = WORD_END.search(old_word + token)
    word = match.group(0)[-40:] if match else ''
    known = float(word in FRENCH_SPELLINGS)
    continues = bool(old_word and token and token[0].isalpha())
    value = 0.0

    if any(c in token for c in CIRCUMFLEX):
        i = max(token.rfind(c) for c in CIRCUMFLEX)
        vowel = token[i]
        following = min(3, sum(c.isalpha() for c in token[i + 1:]))
        preceding = min(4, sum(c.isalpha() for c in token[:i]))

        earlier_accent = float(any(unicodedata.combining(c)
                                  for c in unicodedata.normalize('NFD', earlier)))

                  - 1.63 * known - 2.58 * fr * known
                  + 0.84 * earlier_accent + 0.62 * preceding)

                            'î': 2.50, 'û': 0.08}
        value = (amount + vowel_adjustment.get(vowel, 0.0)) * .5 ** following
    elif continues and any(c in previous for c in CIRCUMFLEX):
        i = max(previous.rfind(c) for c in CIRCUMFLEX)
        tail = sum(c.isalpha() for c in previous[i + 1:])
        if tail <= 1:
            value = (-.25 - .08 * min(len(token), 4) + .52 * tail
                     - .63 * fr + vi - 1.48 * known)
    elif continues and previous.endswith('è'):
        value = -2.82 + .81 * min(len(token), 4) - .61 * fr
    elif continues and 'é' in previous and len(old_word) <= 5:
        i = previous.rfind('é')
        tail = sum(c.isalpha() for c in previous[i + 1:])
        if tail <= 1:

            value = (-.67 + .21 * min(len(token), 4) - .04 * tail

        value = .03 * min(len(old_word), 4)
        if old_word[-1] not in 'aeiouy':

    return (document, word, token, french, vietnamese), float(max(-14, value))

strongly negative for "lv" (solvent, resolve, salva, vulva), negative for "lf", "lp"
(Wolfe, Rudolfo, ALPs), slightly negative for "lb", positive for "lk" and "lc"/"lch"
(solchen, Volker, Alk), and the Cyrillic л+к (ёлку, стал|ки) is positive too. A middle-dot

    same_doc = len(prefix) > 1 and prefix.document_ids[-2] == prefix.document_ids[-1]

after a letter 'v' or 'V' with no space between them: the 1 or 3 in Go module paths

("cn.bmob.v3"), file and identifier names ("tests_v1", "BackendV1", "corev1"), and

rather than on the token, so this program leaves them at 0.

READS = ()

DIGIT_VALUE = {"0": 1.3, "1": 2.8, "2": 3.4, "3": 5.0}

def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    if len(prefix) < 2 or prefix.document_ids[-2] != prefix.document_ids[-1]:

    before = prefix.token_strings[-2]

purpose of", "the possibility of"), where the phrase is idiomatic and the activation is

"levels in patients") and near zero or negative on verb-complement and set phrases

part of that pattern: which word class fires, how strongly, and when it is suppressed by
a fixed phrase. It does not model the finer lexical choice of the previous word, which is
where most of the remaining variance is.

    " all", " every", " some", " many", " my", " these", " that", " our",
}

    " element", " total", " variety", " case", " sense", " capable", " embodiment", " terms",

"""layers.1.mlp.down_proj:2015 — a "German umlaut" detector.

What it does: this component goes strongly negative on the umlaut letters ä, ö, ü
(and Ä, Ö, Ü) when they sit inside a German word, e.g. the "ä" of "Bäcker",
"Gräber", "Ärzte", "gläubig", "Kühe". It is weaker on the letters that follow
such an umlaut within the same word ("Rücksichten": the "cks" after "Rü"), and it
is near zero on umlauts in Turkish, Hungarian, Swedish or English text.

Why the German context matters: the strength depends on how German the surrounding
text is. The program keeps a running, decaying count of common German function words
(der, die, und, ist, nicht, ...) in the current document, and scales the response by
that count (saturating at 3). Common umlaut words that the model already knows well
(für, über, können, müssen, möglich, ...) respond only weakly.

Nothing else is modelled: the component's small residual activity on ordinary
German word fragments is left at 0.
"""

UMLAUTS = set("äöüÄÖÜ")
GERMAN = set(
    "der die und ist nicht das ein eine einen mit sich auch zu von für dem den des im "
    "auf es wir sie ich wird werden oder aber wie bei nach über sind noch kann hat haben "
    "sein dass daß wurde zum zur ihre seine".split()
)
COMMON = set(
    "für über können müssen während zurück möglich Männer täglich häufig würde wäre "
    "hätte höher größer Universität darüber dafür".split()
)
READS = ()


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    # carry: (document id, German-word score, whether the previous token was part of
    # a word that has an umlaut in it so far). None at the start of a row.
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if carry is None or carry[0] != doc:
        carry = (doc, 0.0, False)
    _, german, after_umlaut = carry

    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    word = token.strip()
    has_umlaut = any(ch in UMLAUTS for ch in token)
    german_level = min(german, 3.0) / 3.0  # 0 (not German) .. 1 (clearly German)
    continues_word = token[:1].isalpha()

    if has_umlaut and word in COMMON:
        value = -1.1
    elif has_umlaut:
        value = -(0.3 + 3.6 * german_level)
    elif after_umlaut and continues_word:
        value = -(0.2 + 1.6 * german_level)
    else:
        value = 0.0

    new_german = 0.98 * german + (1.0 if word.lower() in GERMAN else 0.0)
    new_after = has_umlaut or (after_umlaut and continues_word)
    return (doc, new_german, new_after), value

What it does, in plain terms: the component is silent almost everywhere, and fires on the
*name* of a Java annotation, and on capitalised class names pulled in by Java imports:

* The name after an '@' that opens a line is the strongest case: `@Override` (~6-9),
  `@Test` (~9), `@Before`/`@After`, `@Service`, `@Data`, `@RequestMapping`, `@NonNull`,
  `@PathVariable`, ... A '@Name' that is not a known Java annotation, but sits at the start
  of a line, still gets a moderate value; an '@Name' in the middle of a line (social handles,
  e-mail addresses) gets nothing. Lowercase names after '@' (`@param`, `@types`) get nothing.
* In an `import` line, a capitalised class name after the dot gets a small value, and a
  larger one when the package is an annotation or test framework (`org.junit.Before`,
  `org.springframework.context.annotation.Bean`, `androidx.annotation.NonNull`).
* A capitalised tag name right after '<' (component tags such as `<Stack>`, `<Picker>`)
  gets a weak value.

carry, reset at each document boundary.

    "Override": 6.5, "Test": 9.0, "Before": 8.0, "After": 7.0, "Data": 11.0, "Service": 12.0,
    "Component": 9.5, "RequestMapping": 7.5, "ResponseBody": 7.4, "RequestParam": 4.6,
    "PathVariable": 3.0, "NonNull": 3.5, "Nonnull": 4.0, "Generated": 5.0, "FXML": 7.5,
    "SuppressWarnings": 4.2, "RunWith": 4.2, "IBOutlet": 3.7, "Get": 4.0,
}

TAG_VALUE = 1.0                # capitalised name right after '<' (component tags)
IMPORT_CLASS = 1.5             # capitalised class name in an import line
ANNOTATION_IMPORT = 6.0        # ... imported from an annotation or test package

def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    same_doc = len(prefix.document_ids) > 1 and prefix.document_ids[-1] == prefix.document_ids[-2]
    line = (carry or "") if same_doc else ""   # text of the current line so far
    s = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    prev = prefix.token_strings[-2] if len(prefix.token_strings) > 1 else ""
    value = 0.0

        name, at_line_start = s[1:], line.strip() == ""
    elif prev.endswith("@") and NAME.fullmatch(s):      # '@' followed by the name
        name, at_line_start = s, line.rstrip("@").strip() == ""
    else:

    if name is not None:

    elif prev.endswith("<") and NAME.fullmatch(s):

    elif stripped.startswith("import ") and s.startswith(".") and NAME.fullmatch(s[1:]):

        value = ANNOTATION_IMPORT if is_annotation_package else IMPORT_CLASS

"""Layer-1 MLP down_proj component 2017: a year-prefix detector, plus two oddities.

What the component responds to, from the data:
  * The second digit of a year that begins "19" (the '9' in '19xx') is positive,
    about +0.17 on average, and more in prose ("(born 19..", "In the 19..").
  * The '0' of "20xx" is positive, about +0.08.
  * The Chinese character 九 ("nine") when it follows 一 ("one") is the '9' of a
    Chinese year written 一九xx年, and it is strongly positive, about +0.4 to +0.5.
    The highest-importance positions in the data are these.
  * The colon in YAML front matter's "title:" line, right after a document's
    opening '---', is strongly positive, about +0.7.
  * The leader-dot token '··' (a run of middle dots, as in a table of contents)
    is strongly negative, about -1.1 every time it occurs.
Everything else is predicted as 0. The program reads only the newest token and
the few before it, within the same document.

READS = ()

YEAR_20_ZERO = 0.08     # '0' of '20' as digits
JIU_AFTER_YI = 0.41     # 九 after 一: the '9' of a Chinese 19xx year
JIU_OTHER = 0.12        # 九 elsewhere

def _is_digit(text):
    return len(text) == 1 and text.isdigit()


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    tokens = prefix.token_strings
    docs = prefix.document_ids
    n = len(tokens)
    now = tokens[-1]
    prev = tokens[-2] if n >= 2 and docs[-2] == docs[-1] else None
    prev2 = tokens[-3] if n >= 3 and docs[-3] == docs[-1] else None
    value = 0.0
    if now == LEADER_DOT:
        value = LEADER_DOT_VALUE
    elif now == "9" and prev == "1" and not (prev2 is not None and _is_digit(prev2)):
        value = YEAR_19_NINE
    elif now == "0" and prev == "2" and not (prev2 is not None and _is_digit(prev2)):
        value = YEAR_20_ZERO
    elif now == "九":
        value = JIU_AFTER_YI if prev == "一" else JIU_OTHER
    elif now == ":" and prev == "title" and prev2 == "---\n":
        value = TITLE_COLON
    return carry, value

"""A language-gated approximation to recurrent negative spelling spikes.

Completed-word frequencies estimate German or Scandinavian context. German
k/z pieces drive negative values; Scandinavian text has a weaker k response.
Length, German word frequency, neighboring letters, pr/pl starts, and rarity
adjust these values. A weaker response follows into the next piece of a word.
The literal document-initial 'Title:' colon is handled separately. Individual
token amplitudes and split-byte effects are not modeled.
"""
from functools import lru_cache
from wordfreq import zipf_frequency
import re

READS = ()

@lru_cache(maxsize=60000)
def evidence(word):
    if len(word)<2:
        return (0.,0.,0.)
    de=zipf_frequency(word,'de')
    no=max(zipf_frequency(word,l) for l in ('nb','da','sv'))
    other=max(zipf_frequency(word,l) for l in
              ('en','nl','pl','hu','tr','fr','es','it','pt'))
    return (max(0.,de-max(3.,no,other)),
            max(0.,no-max(3.,de,other)),
            max(0.,other-max(3.,de,no)))

def language_step(state,s,doc):
    if state is None or state[0]!=doc:
        state=(doc,'',0.,0.,0.)
    # Leaky totals of German, Scandinavian, and other-language word evidence.
    _,word,g,n,e=state
    for c in s:
        if c.isalpha():
            word=(word+c)[-60:]
        elif word:
            a,b,other=evidence(word.lower())
            g=.93*g+a
            n=.93*n+b
            e=.93*e+other
            word=''
    gs=min(1.,g/3.)*min(1.,(g+.3)/(n+e+.3))
    ns=min(1.,n/3.)*min(1.,(n+.3)/(g+e+.3))
    return (doc,word,g,n,e),gs,ns

@lru_cache(maxsize=60000)
def spelling(token, previous_letter):
    word = token.strip().lower()
    if not word.isalpha():
        return (0.,) * 8
    if not all(c.isascii() or c in 'äöüß' for c in word):
        return (0.,) * 8
    n = len(word)
    frequency = zipf_frequency(word, 'de')
    familiarity = 1.
    if n >= 2 and token[:1].isspace():
        familiarity = min(1., max(.03, (5.3-frequency)/.6))
    scale = familiarity * min(1., 4./n)**2
    if not word.isascii():
        scale *= .4
    joined = previous_letter + word
    k = float('k' in word and 'ck' not in joined) * scale
    z = float('z' in word) * scale
    initial = word.startswith(('k', 'z'))
    e_neighbor = bool(re.search(r'[kz]e', word)) * scale
    closing_cluster = bool(re.search(r'tz|zt|k[st]', joined)) * scale
    vowel_before = bool(re.search(r'[aeiou][kz]', joined)) * scale
    pr_pl_start = (word.startswith(('pr', 'pl')) and n <= 5) * scale
    rarity = max(0., 4.-frequency) / 4.
    return (k, z, initial, e_neighbor, closing_cluster,
            vowel_before, pr_pl_start, rarity)


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if carry is None or carry[0] != doc:
        carry = (doc, None, (0., 0.), 0, '')
    _, language, previous_shape, age, previous_token = carry
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    boundary = not token or token[0].isspace() or not token[0].isalpha()
    previous_letter = ''
    if language is not None and not boundary:
        previous_letter = language[1][-1:]
    language, german, scandinavian = language_step(language, token, doc)
    (k, z, initial, e_neighbor, closing_cluster,
     vowel_before, pr_pl_start, rarity) = spelling(token, previous_letter)
    german_value = (
        k * (-0.953 - 1.651 * initial)
        + z * (-2.515 - 0.803 * initial)
        +1.404 * e_neighbor
        +1.333 * closing_cluster
        -1.093 * vowel_before
        -1.062 * pr_pl_start
        -0.085 * rarity
    )
    value = -0.003 + german * german_value
    value += scandinavian * k * (-0.708 - 0.457 * initial)
    if not boundary:
        previous_k, previous_z = previous_shape
        value += german * (-0.780 * previous_k - 0.969 * previous_z)
        value += scandinavian * (-0.372 * previous_k)
    if age == 1 and previous_token == 'Title' and token == ':':
        value = -5.326
    return (doc, language, (k, z), age + 1, token), float(value)

What it does, in plain terms: this component goes strongly negative on the

document (reset at each new document) and predicts:
  - bare k/z token (k, z, K, Z, with or without a leading space): -3.1

    value += 0.91 * (word in YEAR_WORDS)
    value += 0.62 * (word in MONTHS or word in SHORT_MONTHS)

    cur = prefix.token_strings[-1]

Literal x is strongest in short fragments and capitals. A fragment continuing
an existing word gets a boost. Related letters/signs and Mandarin readings
beginning with x have their own response sizes. The previous x also
raises a following word fragment, digit, or exponent. Document changes reset it.
"""
from functools import lru_cache
from pypinyin import lazy_pinyin
import regex

@lru_cache(maxsize=65536)
def describe(text):
    if text.startswith('<|') and text.endswith('|>'):
        return 0.0, False, False, False, False
    letters = ''.join(c for c in text if c.isalpha())
    lower = letters.lower()
    count = lower.count('x')
    n = len(letters)
    value = 0.005
    if count:
        # A length curve: one letter, two, three, four, 5-6, 7-9, 10+.
        if n <= 4:
            band = n - 1
        elif n <= 6:
            band = 4
        elif n <= 9:
            band = 5
        else:
            band = 6
        value += (1.52, 1.34, 1.13, 0.75, 0.64, 0.43, 0.37)[band]
        value += 0.49 * letters.isupper() + 0.13 * letters.istitle()
        value += 0.10 * lower.startswith('x') + 0.25 * (count - 1)
        value += 0.16 * bool(text and text[0].isspace())
        if text.startswith('\\x') and len(text) > 2:
            value -= 0.43  # Part of a hexadecimal byte escape, not a word.
    value += 0.42 * ('х' in lower) + 4.0 * ('ξ' in lower)
    value += 0.79 * ('χ' in lower) + 1.32 * ('×' in text)
    value += 1.48 * ('خ' in text)
    han = ''.join(regex.findall(r'\p{Script=Han}', text))
    if han:
        readings = lazy_pinyin(han)
        value += 0.40 * sum(p.startswith('x') for p in readings) / len(han)
    digit = any(c.isdigit() for c in text)
    starts_letter = bool(text and text[0].isalpha())
    return value, bool(count), bool(n), digit, starts_letter


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    text = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    previous_x, previous_letter = False, False
    if carry is not None and carry[0] == doc:
        _, previous_x, previous_letter = carry
    value, has_x, has_letters, has_digit, starts_letter = describe(text)
    space = bool(text and text[0].isspace())
    if has_x and starts_letter and previous_letter:
        value += 0.56
    if previous_x:
        if space:
            value += 0.05
        elif has_letters:
            value += 0.56
        elif has_digit:
            value += 0.22
        else:
            value += 0.06
        if text in ('^', '²', '³'):
            value += 0.90
    return (doc, has_x, bool(text and text[-1].isalpha())), float(value)

The component fires on the Latin letter x wherever it shows up in the current
token. A lone "x" or "X", or a short token containing x ("ax", "ix", "box",
"Max", "xml"), fires most, around 1.6. An x inside a longer word ("exit",
"export", "example", "text") fires less, around 0.7. Symbols that look like x
or stand for it also fire: the multiplication sign, Greek chi and xi, and the
Cyrillic letter kha. Special tokens such as <|endoftext|> are excluded even
though their spelling contains "text".

Two small effects around an x: an exponent sign (^ or ²) right after an x, as
in x², fires about 1.0, and the token right after an x-token gets a small
bump of 0.15. Everything else gives 0.

The program reads the current token and the one before it, so it needs no carry.
"""

# Symbols that look like x or stand for it, with their typical activation.
X_SYMBOLS = {"×": 1.3, "χ": 1.0, "ξ": 4.0, "х": 1.0}
SHORT_X = 1.6  # x inside a token of three letters or fewer
LONG_X = 0.7  # x inside a longer word
EXPONENT_AFTER_X = 1.0  # ^ or ² right after an x
AFTER_X = 0.15  # any other token right after an x


def x_strength(token):
    """How strongly one token (decoded alone) carries the letter x."""
    token = token.strip().lower()
    if token in X_SYMBOLS:
        return X_SYMBOLS[token]
    if "<" in token:  # special tokens such as <|endoftext|>
        return 0.0
    letters = "".join(c for c in token if c.isalpha())
    if "x" not in letters:
        return 0.0
    return SHORT_X if len(letters) <= 3 else LONG_X


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    value = x_strength(token)
    if value == 0 and len(prefix.token_strings) > 1:
        same_doc = prefix.document_ids[-2] == prefix.document_ids[-1]
        if same_doc and x_strength(prefix.token_strings[-2]) > 0:
            if token.strip() in ("^", "²"):
                value = EXPONENT_AFTER_X
            else:
                value = AFTER_X

CARRIAGE_RETURN = "\r"
DOT_LEADER = "·"

"""Approximate a preference for C-family control-flow statements.

Most keywords beginning a line or following a statement delimiter are strongest in
brace/semicolon code. Python suites and unparenthesized Go/Rust-style syntax
weaken that response. Case labels and returns are negative. A few conspicuous
punctuation patterns have separate responses, including initial middle-dot runs.
Opening hash marks, periods and digits also have position-specific rules.
Other tokens get a small negative background. Context resets at document
boundaries; only the last 2000 characters are retained.
"""
import re

READS = ()
STATEMENTS = {
    'if': .68, 'for': .45, 'foreach': .56, 'while': .53,
    'switch': .48, 'case': -.18, 'else': .10, 'return': -.06,
    'try': .09, 'catch': .13, 'break': .05, 'do': .06,
}
PYTHON_SUITE = re.compile(
    r'(?:^|\n)[ \t+\-\d]*(?:async )?'
    r'(?:def|class|if|for|while|elif|else|try|except|with|finally)'
    r'\b[^\n]*:\s*(?:\n|$)'
)


def statement_value(text, token):
    word = token.strip()
    if word == 'foreach':
        return STATEMENTS[word]  # This keyword is unambiguously code.
    recent = text.replace('\\n', '\n').replace('\\t', '\t')
    line = recent.rsplit('\n', 1)[-1]
    boundary = bool(re.fullmatch(
        r'[ \t\r\u00a0]*[+\-]?[ \t]*(?:\d+\t[ \t]*)?'
        r'(?://[ \t]*)?', line
    )) or line.rstrip().endswith((';', '{', '}', '``'))
    code = recent[-1000:]
    braces = any(c in code for c in ';{}')
    python = bool(PYTHON_SUITE.search(code) or
                  re.search(r'\b(?:def|elif|lambda)\b|### Python', code))
    unparenthesized = bool(re.search(
        r'\b(?:func|fn)\b|:=|\blet\s+mut\b|'
        r'\b(?:if|for|while)\s+[^()\n{;]+\{', code
    ))
    if boundary and braces and not python:
        value = STATEMENTS[word]
        if word in {'if', 'for', 'while'}:
            if unparenthesized:
                value *= .4 if word != 'for' else .3
            elif not token[:1].isspace():
                value *= .7 if word == 'for' else .85
        return value
    if word in {'else', 'catch'} and line.rstrip().endswith('}'):
        return .10
    if word == 'if' and line.rstrip().endswith('else'):
        return .36
    if word == 'else':
        return -.07
    return -.015 if word in {'if', 'for'} else -.004


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    text = '' if carry is None or carry[0] != doc else carry[1]
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    value = -.07 if not text else -.004
    if token.strip() in STATEMENTS:
        value = statement_value(text, token)
    elif len(token) >= 2 and set(token) == {'·'}:
        value = -1.99 if not text.strip('·') else -.05
    elif not text:
        # Opening punctuation is quite different from punctuation in prose.
        if token.strip() == '.':
            value = -2.82 if token[:1].isspace() else -.20
        elif token in {'#', '##'}:
            value = .235 if token == '#' else .925
        elif token.isdigit():
            value = -.20
    return (doc, (text + token)[-2000:]), value

"""layers.1.mlp.down_proj:2039 -- a control-keyword detector for brace-language code.

What it does
- Fires (about +0.6) on a control keyword that opens a statement in C-family code
  (C, C++, Java, C#, JavaScript, PHP, ...): `if`, `for`, `while`, `switch`, `foreach`.
  "Opens a statement" means the last meaningful character before the keyword is a
  statement end or brace, `;` `{` `}` (spaces, tabs, newlines and line numbers are
  skipped), or the previous word was `else`.
- Stays at 0 for the same words in prose, after `,` or `(`, and in Python, where a
  line before the keyword ends in `:` rather than `;` or a brace.
- Gives the first token of each document a small negative value (-0.07), since with no
  context before it the component reads only that token's identity.
- Everything else is 0.

Why: on the 1024 eval rows the component is mostly diffuse noise (about +-0.03 per
token). Its clearest response is to statement-opening control keywords in brace code.
This program captures that part and nothing finer.
"""

READS = ()
KEYWORDS = {"if", "for", "while", "switch", "foreach"}
BLOCK_ENDS = set(";{}")
KEYWORD_VALUE = 0.6
FIRST_TOKEN_VALUE = -0.07


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    # carry: the last meaningful character of the current document, "" at a document start
    last = carry if carry is not None else ""
    docs = prefix.document_ids
    first = len(docs) == 1 or docs[-1] != docs[-2]
    if first:
        last = ""
    piece = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    word = piece.strip()

    if word in KEYWORDS and last in BLOCK_ENDS:

tokens so far (it never looks ahead):

   source lines, and tables, the run of indentation is followed by a lone space, a
   non-breaking space or a tab, which is where a line number or the indented code starts.

   about 1.5, a tab about 0.75; a space after a single space fires about 1.3.
2. The third digit of a year, 19x or 20x (the "1" in "2015", the "9" in "1995"), where

DOC_START_SPACE = 1.4

"""Layer 1, MLP down-projection component 2043: "I don't know / please help" detector.

What it does: it fires on the word that completes a phrase about not knowing, being
unclear, or asking for help, information or an explanation:
  "not sure", "don't know", "not clear", "unsure", "let me know", "please help",
  "need help", "can you help", "more information", "tell me", "give me".
The strongest responses come when the word follows a negation ("not sure" ~ +7,
"don't know" ~ +4); a request before it ("let me know", "need help") gives a
medium response; a modal ("could help") a weak one. The same words in ordinary
use ("I know that", "to help") stay near zero. Negative values, and the many small
fluctuations elsewhere, are not modelled.

Why: the component's output is what matters. Predicting these words as "uncertainty
or request" lets the model's next-token prediction move the way the real component does
(toward clause openers such as "what", "if", "how").

Main program: `step` looks at the current word and the one or two words before it,
within the same document, and returns a strength from the three tables below.
"""
READS = ()

# Words that name knowing, clarity, or supplying help or information, with rough strength.
WORDS = {"sure": 1.0, "know": 1.0, "unsure": 1.0, "unclear": 1.0, "clear": 0.7,
         "familiar": 0.8, "figure": 0.6, "help": 0.6, "information": 0.6, "context": 0.6,
         "clarify": 0.6, "info": 0.5, "explain": 0.5, "provide": 0.5, "details": 0.4,
         "tell": 0.4, "recall": 0.4, "remember": 0.4, "idea": 0.4, "ideas": 0.4,
         "applicable": 0.4, "check": 0.3, "think": 0.3}
NEGATION = {"not", "no", "never", "without", "cannot", "dont", "nt", "'t", "’t"}  # "not", "don't"
REQUEST = {"let", "me", "need", "needs", "please", "want"}                        # "let me know"
MODAL = {"can", "could", "would", "should", "might", "will", "may"}               # "could help"
GIVE = {"tell", "provide", "show", "give", "help", "send"}                        # "tell me"


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    # The current word and the two before it, ignoring words from an earlier document.
    toks = [s.strip().lower() for s in prefix.token_strings[-3:]]
    docs = prefix.document_ids[-3:]
    word = toks[-1]
    prev = toks[-2] if len(toks) > 1 and docs[-2] == docs[-1] else ""
    prev2 = toks[-3] if len(toks) > 2 and docs[-3] == docs[-1] else ""
    if word == "me" and prev in GIVE:
        return None, 1.2
    if word in ("unsure", "unclear"):
        return None, 3.0
    if word not in WORDS:
        return None, 0.0
    w = WORDS[word]
    if prev in NEGATION or prev2 in NEGATION:
        return None, 5.0 * w
    if prev in REQUEST or (prev == "you" and prev2 in MODAL):
        return None, 3.0 * w
    if prev in MODAL:
        return None, 0.5 * w
    return None, 0.2 * w

"""Function-body openers fire; statement semicolons go negative (layer 1 MLP, unit 2044).

What the component does: it is a "code block opener" detector. Its activation is large and
positive on the "{" (or the Python "):" ending a def line) that opens the body of a function,
method or class, and negative on the ";" that ends a statement. Almost everywhere else it is
near 0, with small noise that no simple rule captures.

The program looks only at the text before the current token:
  * "{" (or ") {" style tokens) whose header line is a function signature: a line that ends in
    ")" or contains func/fn/function/def, or a Python "def ...):" line -> +4.0 (the average is
    about 3.8).
  * "{" after a class, struct, namespace, interface, enum or impl header -> +2.0.
  * "{" after a control keyword (if, for, while, else, try, catch, switch, ...), or in
    non-code text such as LaTeX, JSON or prose -> 0.
  * ";" ends a statement -> -1.0 (about -1.0 on average).
  * ";" plus a newline after an import line -> +1.5; any other ";" plus newline -> +0.3.
  * everything else -> 0.
The header is the text back to the previous brace, so the rule sees the signature line even
when the brace is on the next line.
"""

import re

READS = ()

CONTROL = re.compile(r"\b(if|for|while|switch|catch|else|try|do|foreach|using|lock|elif|except|with)\b")
TYPE = re.compile(r"\b(class|struct|namespace|interface|enum|impl|trait|module)\b")
FUNC = re.compile(r"\b(func|fn|function|def)\b|=>")


def header(prefix):
    """The text before the current token, back to the last brace (or the last 60 tokens)."""
    parts = []
    for t in reversed(prefix.token_strings[:-1][-60:]):
        if "{" in t or "}" in t:
            parts.append(re.split(r"[{}]", t)[-1])
            break
        parts.append(t)
    return "".join(reversed(parts))


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    s = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    if s == ";":
        return carry, -1.0
    if s == ";\n":
        line = header(prefix).split("\n")[-1]
        return carry, 1.5 if "import" in line else 0.3
    if s == ";\\":
        return carry, 2.0
    if not ("{" in s or s.startswith("):")):
        return carry, 0.0
    lines = [x for x in header(prefix).split("\n") if x.strip()]
    last = lines[-1].strip() if lines else ""
    if s.startswith("):"):
        # the Python def line, "def f(x):"
        return carry, 4.0 if "def " in last else 0.0
    if CONTROL.search(last):
        return carry, 0.0
    if TYPE.search(last):
        return carry, 2.0
    if FUNC.search(last) or re.search(r"\)\s*(const\s*)?$", last):
        return carry, 4.0
    return carry, 0.5

"""Chinese 'help' detector, with a small offset at each document's first token.

The component is switched strongly negative on the Chinese characters 帮 and 幫 (both
"help"), and on 邦 and 忙 (busy/hurry), and on words built on them: 帮我, 帮你, 帮忙
get a medium negative value, other words containing 帮 or 幫 (帮助, 帮扶) a small one,
and the English syllable "bang" a moderate one. Everything else is about zero, except
the first token of each document (where the model's positions restart), which sits
slightly below zero on average. The program reads only the current token and whether a
new document has started.
"""

READS = ()

# Activation predicted for the bare help / busy characters and the bang-sounding 邦.
SINGLE = {"帮": -7.0, "幫": -7.0, "邦": -4.0, "忙": -3.0}
# Common two-character words with those characters.
WORDS = {"帮我": -3.0, "帮你": -2.5, "帮忙": -2.5}
# Average activation of a document's first token.
DOC_START = -0.17


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    tok = prefix.token_strings[-1].strip()
    docs = prefix.document_ids
    # First token of a document (or of the row): positions restart here.
    if len(docs) == 1 or docs[-1] != docs[-2]:
        return None, DOC_START
    if tok in SINGLE:
        return None, SINGLE[tok]
    if tok in WORDS:
        return None, WORDS[tok]
    if tok.lower() == "bang":
        return None, -1.0
    if any(c in tok for c in "帮幫"):
        return None, -0.6
    return None, 0.0

"""A spelling-based estimate of the component's response to z.

Scores Polish-style cz/rz/sz/dz spellings, including those divided between
word pieces, and a following continuation piece. Recent Polish
letters, consonant clusters, following y, and distance from z adjust the
score. Pieces beginning with z have a small negative base; timestamp Z
and the split tik|z spelling receive strong negative estimates.
"""
import re
import unicodedata

READS = ()
# Columns: within this piece, split across pieces, following piece.
PAIRS = {
    'cz': (0.75, 1.44, 0.50),
    'rz': (1.59, 2.17, 0.61),
    'sz': (0.12, -0.07, 0.15),
    'dz': (0.83, 2.18, 1.10),
}
# Polish context, preceding cluster, trailing letters, following y.
MODIFIERS = (
    (1.02, 0.04, -0.50, 0.96),
    (1.86, 1.35, -0.50, 2.03),
    (0.47, 0.88, -0.34, 2.80),
)
RZ_BOUNDARY_BONUS = (1.94, 1.46)
BIAS = 0.002
INITIAL = -0.12
Z_PIECE = -0.15
AFTER_Z = -0.01
AFTER_Z_I = -0.48
TIMESTAMP_Z = -7.61
TIKZ = -4.89
AFTER_STOP = -1.12

TIME = re.compile(r'\d{1,2}:\d{2}(?::\d{2})?(?:\.\d+)?$')


def consonant_cluster(pair, before):
    if pair == 'rz':
        return before.endswith(tuple('pbtdkgcfw')) or before.endswith('ch')
    c = before[-1:]
    plain = unicodedata.normalize('NFD', c)[:1]
    return bool(c and c.isalpha() and plain not in 'aeiouy')


def response(role, pair, before, distance, following, polish, initial_rz=False):
    language, cluster, tail, y = MODIFIERS[role]
    value = PAIRS[pair][role] + language * polish
    value += cluster * consonant_cluster(pair, before)
    value += tail * min(4, distance) + y * following.startswith('y')
    if initial_rz:
        value += RZ_BOUNDARY_BONUS[role == 2]
    return value


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if carry is None or carry[0] != doc:
        carry = (doc, '', '', 0., '')
    _, previous, two_back, polish, recent = carry
    raw = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    text = raw.lower()
    polish = max(.97 * polish, float(any(c in 'ąćęłńśźż' for c in text)))
    continuing = bool(text[:1].isalpha())
    value = BIAS + INITIAL * (not previous) + Z_PIECE * text.startswith('z')
    after_pair = False
    for pair in PAIRS:
        k = text.find(pair)
        if k >= 0:
            post = text[k + 2:]
            value += response(0, pair, text[:k], len(post), post, polish)
        if continuing and text.startswith('z') and previous.endswith(pair[0]):
            post = text[1:]
            initial = pair == 'rz' and previous.strip() == 'r'
            value += response(1, pair, previous[:-1], len(post), post,
                              polish, initial)
        k = previous.find(pair)
        crossed = previous.startswith('z') and two_back.endswith(pair[0])
        if continuing and (k >= 0 or crossed):
            after_pair = True
            before = previous[:k] if k >= 0 else two_back[:-1]
            post = previous[k + 2:] if k >= 0 else previous[1:]
            initial = pair == 'rz' and (previous.strip().startswith('rz') or
                                       (crossed and two_back.strip() == 'r'))
            value += response(2, pair, before, len(post), text, polish, initial)
    if continuing and previous.endswith('z') and not after_pair:
        value += AFTER_Z + AFTER_Z_I * text.startswith('i')
    if text.startswith('z'):
        # Unusual z clusters after labial or velar stops.
        value += AFTER_STOP * previous.endswith(tuple('bpgk'))
        value += TIKZ * previous.endswith('tik')
        if raw == 'Z' and previous[-1:].isdigit() and TIME.search(recent):
            value += TIMESTAMP_Z
    return (doc, text, previous, polish, (recent + raw)[-80:]), float(value)

"""Layer 1, MLP down-projection component 2046: a Polish "rz / cz" z-sound detector.

In plain terms: the component responds to the letter z (also ż, ź) according to the
letter just before it. It fires hardest on z after r, the Polish digraph rz as in
"Katarzyna", "Mistrz", "Gorzów", "drzwi", "Andrzej". It fires less on z after c or d
(cz as in "Czy", dz as in "Kłodzko"), and only a little on z after s (sz). z after most
other consonants is slightly negative, and z after a vowel does nothing.

This is much stronger when the text looks Polish: a Polish letter (ą ć ę ł ń ó ś ź ż)
in the last 80 characters of the same document. Outside Polish text the same spellings
give about a third of the value. The later letters of a word that contains such a z get
a small positive value in Polish text. Two small extras: the English "zip" (zip, .zip,
unzip) is negative, and a run of repeated middle dots "··" sits at a steady negative
level.

The program carries the document's recent text (its last 80 characters) and reads each
new token against the characters before it. A new document clears the carry, as the
model's attention does. Its values are the rough average activation of each case, so it
explains roughly a fifth of the variance; the many small, unlabelled activations are not
modelled.
"""

READS = ()

POLISH_LETTERS = set("ąćęłńóśźżĄĆĘŁŃÓŚŹŻ")
Z_LETTERS = set("zżźZŻŹ")
# value of a z-letter by the (lowercased) letter just before it, in Polish text
BEFORE_Z = {"r": 4.5, "c": 2.2, "d": 2.2, "s": 0.6,
            "k": -1.5, "j": -1.0, "m": -1.0, "l": -0.7, "g": -0.8,
            "w": -0.5, "x": -0.4, "f": -0.4, "b": -0.3, "t": -0.2}
NON_POLISH_SCALE = 0.35
WORD_REST = 0.5        # later letters of a word that had such a z, in Polish text


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    if carry is None or prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]:
        carry = ("", False)
    recent, in_hit_word = carry
    polish = any(ch in POLISH_LETTERS for ch in recent)
    text = recent + token

    value = 0.0
    for k in range(len(recent), len(text)):
        ch = text[k]
        if not ch.isalpha():
            in_hit_word = False          # a non-letter ends the word
        elif ch in Z_LETTERS and k > 0:
            before = text[k - 1].lower()
            if before in BEFORE_Z:
                in_hit_word = True
                scale = 1.0 if polish else NON_POLISH_SCALE
                value = BEFORE_Z[before] * scale

    if value == 0.0 and in_hit_word:
        value = WORD_REST if polish else 0.0
    if "zip" in token.lower():
        value = -1.5
    if token == "··":
        value = -1.2
    return (text[-80:], in_hit_word), value
